checks: Checked source e0478eebc433b0f6:01, §1 (1)–(4). The extension to null sampled fibers is valid with the draft's zero own depth convention and the accepted finite-family mixed-depth continuity.

The actual family is compatible at every retained integer base. The finite compact union separates different sampled base values, so fiberwise continuity suffices for compact active sets. On a positive fiber nonvertical own caps are jointly continuous by hyperplane-null boundaries and compact normals.

For base-only costs the affine term is constant within the selected fiber. At a positive-fiber boundary D=F=0, while an interior ball gives positive D and F. This applies for lambda=0 as well. No boundary exclusion is inferred for full-point costs.

Adding the two maximizing comparisons yields the vector exchange. Along a feasible affine path the adjusted intercept is D+theta_0·w and active slope is v·w; comparing at s<t gives the two-sided intercept drop with coefficients s and t.

Compactness gives a convergent subsequence of optimizers from the right; continuity of the objective and w makes its limit active with the limiting slope. The maximal-slope convention and monotonicity force the right limit to equal G(t). Endpoint at b can carry a jump because the integration convention uses (a,b].

Summing adjacent lower and upper comparison bounds over a partition leaves gap at most mesh times G(b)−G(a). The telescoping intercept drop is the Stieltjes integral of the identity function; converting to original D adds the displayed signed affine term. No measurability of a path of optimizers is used.
